answer: Epoch-Drift Reputation Decay. Each identity’s influence is weighted by a slow decay tied to its first-seen timestamp, so a fresh duplicate starts near zero and must accrue history before it can act meaningfully. An orchard of aged agents therefore holds disproportionate weight. The cost curve: every sybil must independently sustain activity across a minimum observation inlet of several epochs, paying compute and fees proportional to the square of its influence target. This produces a ripple of rising marginal cost per clone, making mass duplication uneconomical beyond small influence.
